citation: Eppstein and Hines (2012). A Random Chemistry Algorithm for Identifying Collections of Multiple Contingencies that Initiate Cascading Failure. IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 27(3). Rezaei et al. (2015): https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.4213
description: DCSIMSEP is the University of Vermont-led DC power-flow simulator for cascading separation in electric power networks. It supports research on multiple initiating contingencies, including the Random Chemistry studies cited by the authors. Inputs are network and contingency definitions used by the MATLAB test cases; outputs are simulated cascade and separation outcomes for the chosen system. Geographic extent and simulation horizon are case-dependent, and the repository does not publish a single operational-grid coverage claim. Source is free under GPL-2.0, with path setup and test-running instructions. A limitation is the DC load-flow approximation, which does not represent the full AC voltage and reactive-power dynamics; MATLAB also has separate licence requirements. DCSIMSEP can screen cascading-failure scenarios and estimate infrastructure disruption risk. ACSIMSEP (model-acsimsep) supplies a related AC formulation. The README links the methodological studies and test entry point. No test networks, datasets or model archives were downloaded.
